title: Learned screening links separate heart-disease expression candidates
summary: Separate learned feature screening of acute-infarction and ischemic-heart-failure datasets nominated candidates that were linked through a protein-interaction database. A four-gene score was constructed and evaluated in 27 archived ventricular samples, with a reported AUC of 0.907. The panel was not a shared predictor set across both diseases and does not establish disease progression or a diagnostic test.
ai_technology: LASSO, random forest and support-vector-machine recursive feature elimination
organization: Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

source_review.scope: Primary article full-text bibliographic metadata and relevant computational evaluation Methods/Results: sec2.1, sec2.4, sec2.6, sec3.5. Primary-source caveat and denominator review; candidate-panel identity corrected where relevant.

evidence.ai_role: LASSO, random forest and SVM-RFE separately screened the disease datasets; a subsequent database interaction analysis, rather than shared selection, connected the four represented candidates.
evidence.tested: Three selectors yielded six infarction and twelve heart-failure nominees separately. STRING interactions linked IL1B from the former with TIMP2, IFIT3 and P2RY2 from the latter. The four-gene ROC model was developed/evaluated within 13 heart-failure and 14 control ventricular samples from GSE116250.
evidence.unknown: Disease stages and tissues differ across discovery datasets, and there is no longitudinal post-infarction cohort. The validation data were used to construct/evaluate ROC models; a locked external predictive score is not established. Individual TIMP2 AUC 0.989 and combined AUC 0.907 are reported on this same small dataset; these do not establish causal mechanisms.
